claims.statement: ORNLSlicer uses CMake for compilation, generated headers and settings, tests, install rules, and platform targets, while Nix provides dependency environments, native and cross packages, and AppImage bundling.

The ornlslicerDev shell inherits package dependencies and adds development tools including ccache, pre-commit, documentation tools, debugger and clang tools, Python utilities, and Linux-only NSIS and analysis tools.
The generic CMake preset uses Clang and Ninja Multi-Config in build/generic-llvm-ninja with Debug and Release build presets, while the fast variant enables a unity build in a separate directory.
Production sources, headers, and Qt resources are recursively discovered and compiled into ornlslicer_obj; the GUI application, Windows console target, and focused tests reuse that object library.
ORNLSlicer requires CMake 3.25, C++23, Qt and its declared geometry/data dependencies, requires CGAL Eigen support, and treats OpenMP as an optional optimization.
CTest targets are explicitly declared when ORNLSLICER_BUILD_TESTS is enabled, and the new-impact project regression is present only when its configured local fixture exists.
Compiler caching is enabled by default and prefers sccache over ccache, falling back to uncached builds if neither is found; PCH is enabled by default and unity builds are optional.

Canonical settings YAML is generated into master.conf and setting_inputs.conf, and CMake makes the object target depend on that generation; Nix packaging disables automatic generation and therefore consumes checked-in outputs.
Configure-time build metadata combines version.json, Git revision plus dirty state, configuration kind, and an overridable package type into a generated header.
GUI and successful CLI startup log version, Git revision, configuration, package type, and both runtime and compile-time Qt versions from the configured build metadata.

The Nix package supports native builds and a MinGW Windows package set, supplies platform-specific Qt wrapping or deployment hooks, and installs the app, Windows runtime files, user guide, and templates through CMake.
The x86-64 Linux AppImage runs the packaged Nix closure through a pinned static PRoot launcher that binds its bundled store at /nix, and CI smoke-tests its --help path as non-root.

Windows CI builds the portable Windows package and the deterministic windowsInstaller Nix derivation, then uploads both; NSIS installs the tree under Program Files with uninstall metadata and Start Menu shortcuts.
CI runs nix flake check --all-systems on Ubuntu and macOS and separately packages Linux and Windows artifacts, but the workflow only declares a command-line smoke test for the Linux AppImage.

The generated Codex Linux worktree setup requires Git, Git LFS, and Nix; validates the repository root and preset inputs; pulls LFS assets; configures generic-llvm-ninja through ornlslicerDev without writing the flake lock; and requires the expected CMake cache.
Codex worktree cleanup leaves worktree-local build removal to the worktree lifecycle and deliberately preserves the shared Nix, Git LFS, and ccache stores.

OpenWiki maintenance can be dispatched manually or runs daily at 08:00 UTC, checks out full history, installs its pinned Node and OpenWiki toolchain, and receives provider and connector credentials through repository secrets.

The OpenWiki workflow removes transient run state and creates or updates an openwiki/update pull request even after a generation failure so completed pages are preserved, then propagates the OpenWiki failure as a failing workflow result.
CMake registers settings_file_comparator_tests, settings_manager_tests, and main_toolbar_tests as focused executables linked to ornlslicer_obj and exposes them to CTest under those names.

The application fileset includes bundled CHANGELOG.md and excludes workflow/wiki inputs; CI cache writes are limited to develop pushes and published releases, with synchronous pushes before permanent pins for all four release outputs.

Version preparation infers Conventional Commit bumps, caps MAJOR at 2, requires an explicit minor bump and compatibility note for breaking changes at that ceiling, and defaults to a dry run that only writes version.json on --write.
The Prepare release workflow creates a new version-only release branch and PR, refuses existing branches, and explicitly dispatches CI; maintainers finalize the changelog on the release PR afterward.
Auto-rebase uses an App token and develop checkout while skipping fork PR targets.
CMake rejects unresolved LFS pointers referenced by Qt resource collections during configure and through the object-library resource-validation dependency.
The canonical developer setup restores LFS assets before configuration and supports direnv use flake with per-checkout authorization and a shared multi-config build tree.
CI runs fork PR events while skipping duplicate same-repository PR runs, and does not cancel published-release runs through concurrency.

Release preparation uses release/<version> branches, promotion to main preserves ancestry with a merge commit, and published CI attaches AppImage, installer and portable ZIP downloads after packaging checks.
